steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
summary: Replaces one-shot KV-cache eviction/compression heuristics with a per-document learned compact cache, optimized via test-time training using generic prompts while model weights stay frozen. Costs a per-document training pass at inference time (extra latency and compute before serving, plus engineering complexity for the two-stage distillation procedure), though memory during generation drops by the compression factor. Can fail when the per-document training cost exceeds the cache savings (short documents, single-query workloads), when generic prompts fail to cover the information later questions require, or when serving infrastructure cannot amortize the per-document training across many queries.
rationale: The quality gain at high compression is large and runs on a single GPU with frozen weights, but the per-document test-time training overhead means it only pays off for long documents queried repeatedly, so the reader must validate it against their own workload economics before adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces one-shot KV-cache eviction/compression heuristics with a per-document learned compact cache, optimized via test-time training using generic prompts while model weights stay frozen. Costs a per-document training pass at inference time (extra latency and compute before serving, plus engineering complexity for the two-stage distillation procedure), though memory during generation drops by the compression factor. Can fail when the per-document training cost exceeds the cache savings (short documents, single-query workloads), when generic prompts fail to cover the information later questions require, or when serving infrastructure cannot amortize the per-document training across many queries.
On RULER, the method achieves 96.7% accuracy at 32x KV-cache compression versus 40.0% for the KVZip+ baseline; gains also reported on LongBench and Phonebook Lookup across Qwen3 and MiniCPM5.
